verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026: re-read the Florida Senate bill page for HB 491 (2025) and the House Criminal Justice Subcommittee (26 Mar 2025) and Judiciary Committee (17 Apr 2025) staff analyses of CS/HB 491, stored from flsenate.gov on 14 Oct 2026 and found unchanged by the archiver on 17 Oct 2026. The bill page confirms the title, sponsors, filing date, the c1 version of 26 Mar 2025, the 114-1 House vote, the withdrawal of 3 May 2025 and the 'Died in Rules' action of 16 Jun 2025. The bill text itself was not stored; the summary rests on the staff analyses, which describe the committee substitute section by section and state that they are not an official statement of legislative intent.

title.quote: CS/HB 491: Use of Artificial Intelligence by Governmental Agencies to Detect Concealed Firearms

official_identifier.quote: CS/HB 491: Use of Artificial Intelligence by Governmental Agencies to Detect Concealed Firearms

status.quote: Last Action: 6/16/2025 Senate - Died in Rules

legal_force.quote: Last Action: 6/16/2025 Senate - Died in Rules

summary.quote: CS/HB 491 prohibits a governmental agency from using, or contracting with any other entity to use, artificial intelligence (AI) in conjunction with any camera, video recording, live-streaming device, or similar technology to detect concealed firearms in a public place.

At any location listed in s. 790.06(12), F.S., which specifies the locations that a person with a concealed weapons or concealed firearms license is not authorized to carry a concealed weapon or concealed firearm into.
The bill authorizes an aggrieved party to seek injunctive relief against a governmental agency or other entity under contract with a governmental agency to prevent or remedy a violation.
“Governmental agency” means any state, county, local, or municipal governmental entity or any unit of local government created or established by law.

notes.quote: Removed a criminal penalty for a violation of the prohibition.
Last Action: 6/16/2025 S Died in Criminal Justice
The effective date of the bill is July 1, 2025. (Section 2)

judgment.status_reasoning: The House passed CS/HB 491 114-1 on 24 Apr 2025; the Senate referred it to Rules, indefinitely postponed and withdrew it on 3 May 2025, and it died in Rules on 16 Jun 2025 (last action on the bill page). A bill that died stays 'Proposed' with status 'Lapsed'. Nothing stored shows a later enactment.
judgment.scope_reasoning: An AI-specific bill prohibiting government use of AI to detect concealed firearms in public places; in scope with no note.
judgment.date_reasoning: date_published is the filing date, 10 Feb 2025; date_last_updated is the posting of the committee substitute c1 on 26 Mar 2025, the last version and the one the House passed.
judgment.summary_reasoning: The current summary matches the Judiciary Committee analysis of CS/HB 491 (Section 1): the prohibition on agencies and their contractors, the exceptions for school grounds and the s. 790.06(12) locations, the injunctive relief and the definition of governmental agency. Left unchanged.
